title: $FlexiReg:$ Flexible Urban Region Representation Learning

problem.claim: Urban region representations are used as inputs for downstream tasks such as check-in or crime prediction.

gap.claim: Existing methods use fixed region formations and fixed input region features that may not suit different downstream tasks.

contributions.claim: FlexiReg learns urban region representations flexibly with respect to both urban region formation and input region features.

The model uses spatial grid partitioning, learns grid-cell representations from publicly accessible urban data, and applies adaptive aggregation and prompt learning to tailor representations to region formations and downstream tasks.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on five real-world datasets reportedly show that FlexiReg outperforms state-of-the-art models by up to 202% in accuracy across four diverse downstream tasks.

narrative_sequence.summary: Urban data enables learning region representations for downstream prediction tasks.
Fixed region formations and input features may not fit different downstream tasks.
FlexiReg is proposed to support flexible region formation and input features.
The model represents spatial grid cells using multiple publicly accessible data sources and adapts aggregation and task specialization.
The authors report results across five datasets and four downstream tasks.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the five datasets, four downstream tasks, baselines, or evaluation protocols.
The abstract does not report the absolute accuracy values or explain how the 202% improvement was calculated.
